title: Buddy Burris: Three-Time All-American Guard at Oklahoma
question: Who was Buddy Burris, the Oklahoma guard named All-American three straight years?
answer: Buddy Burris was a Sooners guard from 1946 to 1948 who earned All-America recognition in each of those seasons, reaching consensus status in 1948. He then played three seasons in the NFL with the Green Bay Packers.
summary: Meet Buddy Burris, the Oklahoma guard listed as an All-American in 1946, 1947 and 1948, a consensus pick in 1948, and later a Green Bay Packer.
body: Before Bud Wilkinson's famous winning streaks, Oklahoma already had linemen worth remembering, and Paul "Buddy" Burris was one of the best. He lettered for the Sooners in 1946, 1947 and 1948, lining up at guard on both offense and defense in the era of two-way football.

OU's All-American history lists Burris as an All-American guard in all three of those seasons. Only the 1948 selection carries the consensus designation, meaning the major selectors agreed he belonged among the nation's best. Few players of any era can point to three straight years of national recognition.

His career also overlapped with a turning point for the program. Wilkinson's first Oklahoma team took the field in 1947, and the 1948 Sooners finished with a strong record while the foundation of the later dynasty was being laid. Burris was part of the line that helped carry that early momentum.

The pros noticed too. Green Bay selected him in the fifth round of the 1947 NFL draft, and he played for the Packers from 1949 through 1951, appearing in 28 games over those three seasons. He was later traded to Philadelphia but did not stay in the league.

Burris is sometimes confused with his younger brother Kurt Burris, the 1954 All-American center who is in the College Football Hall of Fame. Buddy deserves his own spot in Sooner lore as one of the first linemen to put Oklahoma's name on All-America lists year after year.
